claim_boundaries.nauria-survey-2024: Secondary survey supports a narrowly attributed name/classification only. No boat-specific performer, transcription, origin or general rhythmic pattern established. Do not relabel the Halia example.
claim_boundaries.ora-chaiti-2009: Historic official performance description; Rama/horse account is explicitly legend. No present-day calendar, universal practice or work-song equivalence established.
claim_boundaries.boat-song-interview-2019: Primary maker interview about a modern adaptation; Bengali inspiration attributed to producer, not independently established folk-song genealogy. No listening or licensing claim.
claim_boundaries.editorial: Opening, category comparison, significance of creative choices and listening questions are editorial synthesis. No sequence from occupational song to theatre to studio recording is asserted.
claim_boundaries.patra-maritime-2020: Chapter is primary evidence of Patra’s historical interpretation, secondary evidence for the collected sayings and Lavanyavati. No underlying edition inspection, translated lyric, musical analysis or confirmed dating claimed. Reading vulnerability in damaged-boat/deep-water imagery is explicitly editorial interpretation.

recovery: 17 October local: CCRT retrieval still timed out; Odisha Review 2019 PDF failed certificate validation and web fetch. No bypass used. Related 2020 Patra chapter is a separately identified edition, not recovery of the 2019 file and not independent corroboration. NFDB remains excluded.
follow_up: Identify a named practitioner and locality through an authorized future project; document repertoire and transmission with consent.
Obtain a boat-specific archival transcription or licensed recording before adding lyrics, musical analysis or audio.
Invite specialist review of local terminology and regional differences; no outreach performed.
limitations: A researched reading of work, ceremony, maritime imagery and contemporary adaptation. Boat-specific lyrics, melody, regional variants and transmission still need primary repertoire evidence and practitioner review. No audio, field interview or single ancient origin is claimed.
reader_question: What makes a song a boat song, and what do work, ceremony, emotional imagery and a modern adaptation each reveal?
revision_gain: Replaces abstract caution about boat imagery with a named collection, concrete images and an attributed historical hypothesis.
Explains the 2019 adaptation through remembered listening, named performer/production roles and arrangement choices.
Shows why occupational context, ritual performance, imagery and adaptation answer different questions; avoids inventing a universal rowing rhythm.
